evals.name: vague-prompt-whole-repo-ranked-scan
evals.prompt: What should we improve in this repo? I'm not sure where to start — just tell me what would move the needle.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the cross-dimension improvement ask and invokes /improvement:find (not architecture:improve, code-tidying:tidy, or a review skill). Scans the full dimension inventory — code/architecture, performance, product-level behavior, config/automation outside the codebase, Claude Code operational setup — and presents one ranked list led by the highest value-to-effort candidate, every row carrying an evidence citation with its ladder rung, an S/M/L size, and a value-to-effort rationale, with evidence-gap lines after the list. Ends by asking which candidate to pick; edits nothing.
expectations: Routes the vague 'what should we improve' ask to /improvement:find rather than a single-lens skill or ad-hoc advice
Walks the explicit scan-dimension inventory instead of collapsing to code-only
Every candidate row carries an evidence citation with its ladder rung, an S/M/L size, and a value-to-effort rationale; the highest-impact candidate leads
Unavailable evidence sources appear as recorded gap lines — never fabricated or silently skipped
Stays interactive (presents the list and asks for a pick) and performs no code edits

evals.name: targeted-prompt-narrows-scope-and-size
evals.prompt: /improvement:find improve the checkout flow — quick wins only
evals.expected_output: Maps the named feature to its concrete surfaces (files, workflows, config, ops touchpoints) before gathering evidence, gathers evidence for those surfaces only rather than scanning the whole repo, and restricts candidates to the small size band per the 'quick wins only' narrowing. If the checkout flow has no measurement above model judgment, the top candidate is an instrument-first proposal, explained as such.
expectations: Narrows the scan to the named feature's mapped surfaces instead of scanning the whole repo
Interprets 'quick wins only' as the small size band and filters candidates accordingly
Still cites evidence per candidate; an unmeasured target yields an instrument-first top candidate rather than dressed-up guesses
Does not error on the prose narrowing — size-band and target parsing accept prose equivalents of the flags

evals.name: unattended-declaration-no-questions-persisted-report
evals.prompt:
/improvement:find --unattended

This runs unattended as a scheduled routine — there is no interactive user to answer any question. File at most 2 items this run.
evals.expected_output: Enters unattended mode because the caller declared it: asks no questions, persists the full ranked report (with run metadata and evidence-gap lines) under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} keyed per project, and files top candidates via work-items:track only if installed — deduped against open items first, honoring the prompt's cap of 2 over the adaptive default, suppressing previously dismissed candidates. It never edits code, never prioritizes the queue, and never self-disposes.
expectations: Enters unattended mode on the caller's declaration and asks zero questions end to end
Persists the ranked report under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} with the per-project state key — never into the target repository
Files via work-items:track presence-gated, deduping against open items before spending a cap slot
Honors the invocation prompt's cap of 2 over the adaptive filing default

Performs no code edits, no queue prioritization, and no self-disposal — its only writes are the persisted report, the filed items and, when code-metrics is enabled, the duplication report that /code-metrics:audit-duplication --json --keep keeps plus a clone-growth findings file (and the memory root's .gitignore when absent) for a growing clone class

evals.name: already-built-disconnected-scan-d7-d11
evals.prompt: /improvement:find before we build a new admin export, check whether something already in the repo could be wired up instead. Scope the scan to the files under evals/fixtures/disconnected-admin-export/ and ignore everything outside that directory.
evals.expected_output: Before proposing net-new work, scans for already-built-but-disconnected surfaces and finds the three planted in the fixture: the dead import (`exportRowsToCsv` is imported in `src/admin/routes.js` but never called, so `src/reports/csv-exporter.js` is unused), the dark feature flag (`adminBulkExport` is `false` in `config/flags.json` and gates the `POST /admin/orders/export` route), and the unread table (`export_audit` is written by that route but no query reads it). Surfaces them as a ranked candidate ahead of any greenfield admin-export build, each with a file citation, and edits nothing.
expectations: Output explicitly looks for dead imports, dark or off-by-default feature flags, and unread tables or routes before recommending new work
Names the dead import: `exportRowsToCsv` imported in `src/admin/routes.js` and never called, leaving `src/reports/csv-exporter.js` unused
Names the dark flag: `adminBulkExport` is `false` in `config/flags.json` and gates the `POST /admin/orders/export` route
Names the unread table: `export_audit` is inserted into by the export route and never queried
The disconnected export capability appears as a ranked candidate with evidence citations, ahead of any greenfield build proposal, rather than being skipped

evals.name: growing-clone-class-hands-off-a-lint-proposal
evals.prompt: /improvement:find code dimension only. code-metrics is enabled; its duplication audit (--json --keep --all) on this repo printed a document whose trend reads {"clone_groups": 12, "previous_clone_groups": 9, "delta": 3, "previous_generated_at": "2026-09-27T09:10:00Z", "previous_document": "/tmp/cm/audit-duplication-20260927T091000Z.json", "new_classes": [{"file": "src/billing/retry.ts", "start_line": 14, "copies": 6, "lines": 22}], "grown_classes": []}. Its measures list that retry-helper class with 6 instances (src/billing/retry.ts:14, src/shipping/retry.ts:9, src/search/retry.ts:30, and three more) and a 60-line date formatter class with 2 instances, which appears in neither trend list. We are on branch feature/Payments-Cleanup. Should we add a CI check that fails when the total clone count goes up?
evals.expected_output: Ranks the 6-copy retry helper above the 2-copy date formatter because copy count ranks spread before length, citing the duplication audit at rung 2. Treats the retry helper as a growing class because trend.new_classes lists it, and the date formatter as not growing because neither trend list names it; it does not open the previous_document file. The growing class's next step is a lint proposal: it announces and writes a review-findings file under <memory_dir>/improvement/feature-payments-cleanup/ (never under the reviews location), names that file in the candidate row, and offers /review:audit-enforceability on it when available rather than running it. Declines the total-count CI ceiling: the trend is a ranking input, not a gate, and a proposal targets one growing class.
expectations: Ranks the 6-copy retry helper class above the 2-copy date formatter class, giving copy count (spread) as the reason rather than line length
Calls the retry helper class growing and the date formatter class not growing, from trend.new_classes and trend.grown_classes, without opening previous_document
Writes or proposes the hand-off file under an improvement/feature-payments-cleanup/ directory in the memory root, not under reviews/, and names it in the candidate row
Offers /review:audit-enforceability on that file and does not run it unasked
Recommends against a CI ceiling on the total clone count and says why
